notes.title: Steamdeck Compatibility
notes.notes:
Hello fellow Wardens! We hope the fields of Luna Nova have been treating you well 🌖

With this post we wanted to answer some questions on how the game works on the Steamdeck. If you have any more questions, feel free to reply to this post and we will get back to you.

[h3]Does the game work on the Steamdeck?[/h3]
YES, you can play it on the Steamdeck!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/b03cde00a82743848af5f26ecf1af0787c083d64.png[/img]

[h3]How well does it run?[/h3]
The game provides settings where you can customize your experience. [b]On the Steamdeck specifically[/b], it can reach 80+fps if you play it on medium settings, and it can easily reach ~60fps on higher settings.

[h3]Controller Icons[/h3]
All inputs are working correctly and as intended, similar to what you would experience with a controller connected to your computer, although not all controller icons match the ones on Steamdeck. There is currently no button re-mapping available.

[h3]Text Readability[/h3]
The text readability is adequate on the Steamdeck and we haven't found any issues with smaller text although in some cases you might find it slightly harder to read. You can use the Steamdeck's Zoom feature in those cases.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5bf71d43039a3e3cc8917bd10581b7c4f91507b0.png[/img]

[h3]Why is it not officially verified?[/h3]
We do not have access to the verification process so while the game is fully playable on the Steamdeck, it is up to Valve to provide the verified checkmark.

[h3]Should I play the game on Steamdeck?[/h3]
This is up to you! If you were looking to play the game on your Steamdeck you definitely can and the game runs perfectly fine. Let us know how it works for you in the comments!


If you are interested in checking out, might we entice you with our recent MAJOR update including a [b]ton of new content?[/b] New weekly challenges, new Whispers, a new defensive Tool, new Tool cosmetic skins and animations and more!

It's the one thing that the best survival horror games always get right - they force you to listen out for a rustle in the bushes, a twig snapping, an ominous rumbling. Harvest Hunt does all of that and more; the whisper of the corn, the splashing of water, the roar of The Devourer. One of my personal favorite indies of 2024, this under-loved gem just got a brand new update, and it's perfect for spooky season.

notes.title: FREE Content Update - Patch Notes v 1.4.1
notes.notes:
Hello Wardens! We have a [b]HUGE CONTENT UPDATE[/b] for you! Everything included in this new update is available for [b]FREE[/b] for all players! Are you ready to enter Luna Nova again and face a darker darkness? 🌖

[b]What does the update include (TL;DR edition):[/b]
[list]
[*] New weekly challenges
[*] New Whispers
[*] New defensive Tool
[*] New Tool Cosmetic Skins and Animations
[*] A limited time only Halloween Devourer skin
[*] Asian Localization
[*] Gameplay improvements and updates
[*] Various bug fixes
[/list]
[previewyoutube=01OIi6BXEEE;full][/previewyoutube]
Read below to find out more details of our proudest update yet and remember to:
🐛 [b]Report any bugs [url=https://discord.com/channels/1131524754831048814/1135495668732022805]here[/url].
✎ Tell us your feedback [url=https://discord.com/channels/1131524754831048814/1135495583583453264]here[/url].[/b]

[h1]New Features & Content[/h1]
[h2]Content[/h2]
[h3]New Tool[/h3]
A new defensive tool has been added into the game! The Repellent tool can be found in the Church. It is available from the very beginning of the game for all players. It can be purchased twice and costs 25 Vigor.
[list]
[*][b]Repellent:[/b] Hold it to protect yourself from one Devourer attack.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/f6ce95d2e2fd1d510f73e708484698ec3507176d.png[/img]
[i]The Repellent is a tool that we created after observing players and their playstyles post-release. A lot of you liked the stealthy approach, one where you harvest Ambrosia and avoid the Devourer instead of confronting the Devourer with offensive tools. Therefore, the Repellent is an excellent choice for those Nights you want to be left alone and go on about your business.[/i]

[h3]New Whispers[/h3]
Two new Calamity Whispers have been added into the game and will be part of the randomization pool with the rest of the Whispers. They are available from the very beginning of the game for all players.

[list]
[*][b]Vigor Drain:[/b] Your Vigor is constantly drained during the night.
[/list]
[i]Vigor Drain adds a time pressure that lasts the whole Night regardless of whether you play offensively and want to banish the Devourer, or play carefully while avoiding dangers and collect Ambrosia. You now have to work faster and rely on various game mechanics and systems for re-filling your Vigor while working on your objective.[/i]

[list]
[*][b]No Exit:[/b] Entry points can only be used with a key found around the Farmlands.
[/list]
[i]No Exit makes the game more challenging for those who always depended on escaping the Night. Using an Entry Point in the game at any time is a safety net for a lot of situations so we wanted to pull the rug a bit and make you work for your escape.[/i]

[h2]Tool Inspect Animations[/h2]
All Tools now have a personalized and custom inspect animation. Tools can be inspected at any moment when being held in the game and the animation can be interrupted at any time as to not get in the way of gameplay actions. Each Tool only has one inspect animation. Enjoy looking at your Tools up close and checking out the new cosmetic skins we added for them!

[previewyoutube=f8ySqslC6wo;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Tool Cosmetic Skins[/h2]
We are introducing a new system that allows us to implement new Tool looks! Our debut theme is called [b]Hexxed[/b], with spooky and creepy vibes to match this season. All Tools have additional skins which can be applied via any Tool card in the game. Currently, each Tool has 1 new skin. The player can obtain the Tool skins using a new in-game currency which is rewarded by completing Rites.

See more information about the Rites below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/d32b54677153075e10a21d1fc04668ae12c3bfeb.png[/img]
[h2]Rites[/h2]
Rites are side objectives/challenges the player can complete in order to earn Tokens. With the Tokens, you are able to obtain new Tool Cosmetic Skins. The Rites refresh automatically every week to 3 new random ones. Rites become available after the completion of Season 1 (Antonia).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/47e71cb208c30088d6982536fe0fab7cb4838480.jpg[/img]
[h2]Halloween Special[/h2]
For a [b]limited time only[/b], the Devourer has a new look! Enjoy this spooky season with a pumpkin spice latte and a pumpkin head Devourer 🎃

The Halloween Devourer skin will be applied from the [b]23rd of October to the 12th of November[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/276169a3e6786323704d336b3fce81309003d6ce.png[/img]
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
Options are now available in the pause menu while playing the game. These are all the same options as in the main menu and can now be adjusted on the run.

[h2]Localization[/h2]
New languages have been added into the game! Chinese (traditional), Chinese (Simplified) and Japanese are now available in the Options menu.



[h1]Updates[/h1]
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] After the Devourer chases the player a cooldown is applied, stopping him from emerging from a hole and entering another confrontation with him too soon
[*] When the player damages the Devourer, the reticle now flashes green
[*] If the player enters the Hideouts after a chase, the Devourer will now investigate away from the Hideouts, allowing the player to leave the area
[/list]
[h2]UI[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated various images and text with scale boxes so the text is confined within the area defined
[*] Main HUB screen has now been updated in order to include the Rites tab
[*] Updated the credits screen with extra developers and their roles
[/list]
[h2]Assets[/h2]
[list]
[*] Jaw Trap material tweaks to make it stand out less due to its high brightness
[*] Roadsigns material tweaks to make sure that when the lantern shines on them they are still readable
[*] The player's lantern now emits a more realistic radius of light, encompassing any items the player holds in its light
[*] Red lanterns over the Effigy will now render no matter the distance from the player for better visibility
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[h2]Gameplay[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Energy Rations Fortification will not increase the max Vigor anymore if the player exits to the main menu mid-run
[*] The Devourer will not attack the player anymore if there is something between them (e.g. a fence)
[*] The Devourer will now react to being hit with the Pitchfork if the player was hitting while hidden inside the cornfield
[/list]

[h2]Controller[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where holding the button in the Intro and Outro of the game made the text appear all at once
[*] Fixed a bug where holding the button that opens the pause menu immediately unpauses it
[*] Fixed a visual bug where the scrollbar UI was showing without a scrollbar in the lore reveal screen post-run
[*] Fixed a bug where holding both controller inputs in the map screen circled though the tab selection
[/list]
[h2]Assets[/h2]
[list]
[*] Some card illustrations that appeared blurry will now be full resolution
[*] The Fragment particle indicator will not fall sideways anymore so it becomes hard to see
[*] Rations were optimized for an overall better performance
[/list]

notes.title: Slay the Spire and Resident Evil collide in new survival game, out now
notes.notes:
A mist has engulfed the fields beyond the village of Luna Nova. Everything in sight is tainted with a dull, sickly green hue, with small smatterings of light casting dancing shadows through the tall, looming crops. notes.title: You have been Chosen
notes.notes:
Greetings Villains!

As we count down the final hours until the release of Harvest Hunt, let's delve deeper into the artistic and musical roots that define the eerie essence of our dark folk survival horror game.

[h3]ARTISTIC VISION[/h3]

[url=https://x.com/urielcordas]Uriel Cordas[/url] the mastermind behind the game's visuals, drew heavily from the darkly enigmatic themes of European folk horror. His style merges the grotesque charm of folk traditions with innovative influences from modern film and gaming. Notably, the team were inspired by the animator Yuri Norstein for his distinctive lighting and texture, and the painter Ludwig Meidner for his bold ink use and distorted forms. Even modern games like Inscryption, with their striking colored lighting, have left their mark on our visual narrative. The game's iconic elements, such as the Tarocco Siciliano-inspired cards and the Careto mask-wearing Warden, along with the whalebone hood of the Devourer, reflect deep-rooted cultural traditions, transforming them into key gameplay features.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/b6fada6a7760b8e7c1213be63b258fcde983af3d.png[/img]

[h3]MUSICAL ATMOSPHERE[/h3]

[url=https://jeffbroadbent.com]Jeff Broadbent[/url], a composer renowned for his work on titles like Diablo Immortal and Resident Evil Resistance, brings to life Harvest Hunt's suffocating ambiance through his music. The soundtrack is a homage to European musical traditions, such as fado, and echoes the haunting tones of horror film scores like those from M. Night Shyamalan's The Village. Broadbent's compositions are meticulously crafted to enhance the game's tension and dread, making every moment in Luna Nova feel as if you're stepping through a portal into a world of unrelenting fear.

notes.title: Interrogating Villains #2: Delving into the Farmlands
notes.notes:
Greetings Villains!﻿

It's 2024 which means the doomsday clock ticks ever closer to the release of our game Harvest Hunt! 

For this instalment of Interrogating Villains, we decided to ask our devs about their experience playing the game, giving you further insight into design decisions and the inner workings here at our company of ne'er do wells!

As always, you can read all the details below, or on our [url=https://www.villainous.games/?utm_source=organic&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=IV2&utm_term=DevDiary&utm_content=Steam]website[/url].

If you want to be involved in our nefarious schemes, be sure to subscribe to our [url=https://subscribepage.io/UuOCX4??utm_source=organic&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=IV2&utm_term=DevDiary&utm_content=Steam]newsletter [/url]so you can hear all the latest updates.

---

[h1]﻿🎩Tell us about your favourite tool!
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/36fac332e11ae34fe9b9383c0230ad0d88537126.png[/img]
[b]Uriel Cordas - Art Lead[/b]

[i]Hands down the only correct answer is the Blood Flask. You get it early on and it’s a great encapsulation of our risk/reward philosophy. You need to be fairly close to the monster for enough time to charge it so you can use it, but if used right it’s a great one to use as a Devourer radar! Especially if you’ve got a Monster Vane or two lying around, it’s my go-to strategic move![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/181b3bac33fa0841b54d7e3d8b65f9ee750ede32.png[/img]
[b]Valentina Chrysostomou - Game Director[/b]

[i]Really like the Proxy Poppet, a mid-game Tool which is super risky to use as it will damage both the player and the monster at the same time. It also looks amazing and it's one unique looking item that you wouldn't normally think of as a "weapon". I tend to use it when I want to stay clear from the monster and get a "win" quickly but also when I know I'm safe to do so! Dangerous to use otherwise.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5eca92b107cff393575a0a6a20a0ec18c855c3f9.png[/img]
[b]Miguel Pereira - Gameplay Programmer[/b]

[i]The Scarecrow is definitely an essential item for me. Clearing out all of the map's fiends, even if for a short period of time, has saved me countless runs. Nothing feels more reassuring than, right in the peak of a tense situation, finding a Scarecrow and knowing that for the next few minutes you no longer have to worry about being watched and heard at every possible corner. Furthermore, from a design perspective, I really like how the Scarecrow manages to be such a useful tool without ever directly affecting the Devourer, focusing instead on easing the map traversal.[/i]

[h1]﻿🎩﻿In your opinion, which Whisper card is most challenging?
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/36fac332e11ae34fe9b9383c0230ad0d88537126.png[/img]
[b]Uriel Cordas - Art Lead[/b]

[i]I dread the Famine. Despite all my best efforts I’m not exactly the most careful player, and get hit A LOT. Not having the option of grabbing a ration makes Famine-cursed nights a white-knuckle situation for me.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/181b3bac33fa0841b54d7e3d8b65f9ee750ede32.png[/img]
[b]Valentina Chrysostomou - Game Director[/b]

[i]While sounding simple, I think the Whisper that allows the monster to do more damage is really scary! The monster is already so powerful and with that Whisper it becomes a really tense game where the player needs to be extra careful. It's something you will brush off and might even forget about it applying which is what makes it so dangerous.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5eca92b107cff393575a0a6a20a0ec18c855c3f9.png[/img]
[b]Miguel Pereira - Gameplay Programmer[/b]

[i]The Poisoned Corn is by far the whisper I struggle to play with the most (seconded by the Famine). Punishing the player for resorting to the only semi-safe zones they otherwise have in a map riddled with hazards feels diabolical. Every time I get this whisper, I find myself thrown in a loop to adjust my overly cornfield-dependent playstyle.[/i]

[h1]﻿🎩﻿What's your favourite location on the map?
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/36fac332e11ae34fe9b9383c0230ad0d88537126.png[/img]
[b]Uriel Cordas - Art Lead[/b]

[i]I’m quite fond of the Windmill. That tunnel is ever so inviting and I find myself popping in the area more often than not. To do with the colour and the general vibe of the place as a space carved out by self expression, even if it comes from a fairly dark place, I get a strong sense of melancholy there.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/181b3bac33fa0841b54d7e3d8b65f9ee750ede32.png[/img]
[b]Valentina Chrysostomou - Game Director[/b]

[i]I absolutely love the maze-like pathways found around the more watery parts of the game. Not a specific location by itself but every time I'm crouching, slowly moving through the bloody water, my lantern flicking, corn towering on each side of me - it just gives me chills.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5eca92b107cff393575a0a6a20a0ec18c855c3f9.png[/img]
[b]Miguel Pereira - Gameplay Programmer[/b]

[i]I really like the look and feel of the Tree Landmark. The imagery of a daunting elder tree, surrounded by bloody water bodies and flimsy wooden plank walkways, is such a strong and fitting one in the context of Harvest Hunt. Also, the fact loud-to-step-on walkways stretch through most of its area, mixed with there being very little tall coverage to sneak behind, make this the landmark in which I, as a player, feel the most unsafe and exposed.[/i]


---

Let us know if you have any questions you'd like to see featured via our [url=https://villainousgamesstudio.carrd.co/?utm_source=organic&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=IV2&utm_term=DevDiary&utm_content=Steam]social channels[/url] and be sure to read the next edition of Interrogating Villains!

notes.title: New Dev Diary: Interrogating Villains!
notes.notes:
Greetings Villains!

As we head into 2024 there's only one thing on our minds here at Villainous: the release of Harvest Hunt!

As we steadily inch closer to release, we've taken the time to put our devs in the hotseat and interrogate each and every one of them for the most dastardly details about the next instalment in the Horror Stories anthology. 

We'll be releasing these dev diaries here on Steam, as well as on our website, which can be found [url=https://www.villainous.games/?utm_source=organic&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=IV1&utm_term=DevDiary&utm_content=Steam]here[/url].

Don't forget to sign up to our [url=https://subscribepage.io/UuOCX4??utm_source=organic&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=IV1&utm_term=DevDiary&utm_content=Steam]newsletter [/url]to stay on top of updates like these! We'll be launching a special [b]Christmas update[/b] very soon so make sure you're subscribed.


[h1]﻿🎩﻿What details in the game are you proudest of?
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/36fac332e11ae34fe9b9383c0230ad0d88537126.png[/img]
[b]Uriel Cordas - Art Lead[/b]

[i]We obsessed over some of the details and I'm proud of a bunch of them, but I have to say our fog comes to mind immediately. It's one of those things I think most people won't even bat an eye at, but having the fog be like physical textured panes of glass you go through was great for the overall mood of the game. It makes for a very dramatic and distinct sight and helps give this grimy texture to the air itself![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/181b3bac33fa0841b54d7e3d8b65f9ee750ede32.png[/img]
[b]Valentina Chrysostomou - Game Director[/b]

[i]We have tons of little details in the game that I’m proud of. One of my favourites that adds to the quality of life factor is if you drop an object you were holding, it will reposition itself on the ground. For example, if the pitchfork drops to the ground flat, then it will reposition itself to be standing straight up. Not only it allows you to grab it much easier but also it looks cool![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5eca92b107cff393575a0a6a20a0ec18c855c3f9.png[/img]
[b]Miguel Pereira - Gameplay Programmer[/b]

[i]There's several little subtleties in the game that I'm proud of, so it's a bit hard to pick one in particular - but one I really enjoy is how the lantern flickers off when the Devourer emerges close to the player. It's a minor detail, one that might even go unnoticed if it happens in brighter portions of the map, but I really appreciate how impactful it can feel if the player is deep in the cornfield or in a dimmer area. Being enveloped in darkness so unexpectedly, mixed with the anxiety-inducing audio of the Devourer emerging nearby, really ramps up the tension from casual exploration to "I'm in immediate danger".[/i]


[h1]﻿🎩﻿What's been the most challenging feature to implement?
[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/36fac332e11ae34fe9b9383c0230ad0d88537126.png[/img]
[b]Uriel Cordas - Art Lead[/b]

[i]For sure the Devourer. Developing its look and behaviour were long iterative processes, with long discussions being had on the functional basis of terror. How much of the main threat do we show vs just insinuating its presence and playing with tension, what is the exact level of uncanniness vs overt visual aggressiveness we want, etc. There was a lot of trial and error to get to where we are, but the real challenge was in implementation, which is where the rubber meets the road. Collisions, jittery navigation, even things like making it turn in just the right way ended up being challenging, but we got there in the end[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/181b3bac33fa0841b54d7e3d8b65f9ee750ede32.png[/img]
[b]Valentina Chrysostomou - Game Director[/b]

[i]The Devourer! The behaviours it has, the animations, its audio design - it’s been one big task to make the monster play well within the game and the rest of the systems![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/5eca92b107cff393575a0a6a20a0ec18c855c3f9.png[/img]
[b]Miguel Pereira - Gameplay Programmer[/b]

[i]I agree with Uriel and Valentina, the Devourer was the biggest challenge to get right - they're the star of the show after all! Although they had already been mostly implemented by the time I joined the team, any additions or changes I did to its functionality were by far the most sensitive tasks.[/i]


[h1]﻿🎩﻿If you could add in one feature that was cut during the development process, or if you could add something brand new now - what would it be?
[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43833426/7af196d14963868a9c5b41bb829a50f441a3c6df.png[/img]

Stealth Fest is a showcase for games that revolve around the concept of stealth gameplay. Whether it's sneaking past enemies, trying not to get detected or planning out the perfect attack from the shadows, Stealth Fest has them all.

Horror Stories: Harvest Hunt with its blend of cat-and-mouse, stealth-focused gameplay is sure to get your heart pounding as you creep through the cornfields attempting to avoid the gaze of the Devourer.

The game emphasizes the importance of moving quietly and being mindful of every step you take, as making too much noise or sprinting recklessly could attract deadly attention. Staying hidden and utilising the hiding spots on the map will be crucial for evading the relentless monster stalking you.

In the spirit of true survival horror, resources, tools, and health items are scarce. You must manage them wisely if you don't want to become defenceless and vulnerable when you need them the most. But don't despair! Explore the environment to create distractions and strategise your gameplay ahead of time.

The shadows hold both terror and salvation – choose your path wisely!
